newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil in contango for first time since Augus.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil in contango for first time since Augus.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures slipped into contango for the first time since August on Monday, as the end of strikes at Elf refineries in France and the spectre of Iraqi oil exports pressured prices lower.
The December/January spread stood around -$1.50 at 1620 GMT against last Monday's $4 premium.
"The premium came off very gently over the past week, 25 cents here, 70 cents there, so I think a lot of people were caught out," said one trader.

"If it had come in more quickly I think a lot more people would have have got out before," he added. "But because it happened so slowly a lot of players decided to hold on over the weekend on the expectation it would widen again."
Many traders said weakness in the front month was sparked partly by the the end on Friday of the eight-day strike at three Elf refineries in France which had helped prices higher on supply concerns.

Some said the imminent sale of Iraqi oil for the first time in six years following U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali's approval of the oil-for-food deal -- which envisages the sale of $2 billion worth of oil over six months -- was also a factor.
There was also talk that a Wall Street trader had taken a big position on the January gas oil contract which was keeping it stronger in relation to December.
A few traders said the contango went beyond a response to recent news and was a sign the market was beginning to tire at recent high levels.
"The market's getting exhausted. It can only keep heading up for so long," said another trader. "The end of the strike may have been a catalyst but not necessarily the reason."
"December expires on Thursday." he added. "It will be interesting to see what happens to the Jan/Feb spread then."
